# Independent audit of the free-mass raw-moment selector obstruction

Audited `candidate e16770c76630ebf6` and ran its Fraction verifier: PASS.

The four widths (2,16,17,1) have decreasing first differences, giving precisely the claimed compatible fibers. Fixed fiber-mass endpoint rearrangement gives the displayed strictly concave joint p,q objective for the raw width, with equal masses and the two independent base balances. At both interior integer bases every listed equality multiplier cancels the constraints, and the bound residuals have the correct signs. The negative definite quadratic remainder proves global optimality and uniqueness, including optimization over the common mass. The exact moments, source masses, interval widths, and selected centroids agree with the displayed values. The joint maximum is strictly at base 1, which is an eligible marginal median. All four candidate points have the stated closed bad caps, and the strict deficits are correct.

One additional check connects the example with the interior free-mass John stationarity theorem. At base 1, the unnormalized support directions +1 and -1 have mass coefficients b_+=-31/4 and b_-=31/4, respectively. Thus their equally weighted sum is zero, as the free-mass stationarity requires. Their hinges are 1825/32 and 1187/32; the raw John radius is 753/16, so their John-normalized average hinge is exactly one. The geometric stationarity therefore holds while the selector fails depth; there is no conflict between these facts.
